description.value: The study investigated whether a bitter wormwood-tea aftertaste changes neural and affective responses to visual food cues in healthy, normal-weight women using repeated-measures fMRI, and whether appetite reduction correlates with brain activation.

spans.text: In the current fMRI study, healthy, normal-weight women were presented with images depicting high-caloric and low-caloric food, once in combination with a bitter aftertaste (wormwood tea) and once with a neutral taste (water).

description.value: The study had a repeated measures design. The participants were invited to two fMRI sessions separated by approximately one week, during which they either received wormwood tea or water. The sequence of the conditions was counterbalanced.
